app.always_run_as_administrator_help: GCM starts with administrator rights without a UAC prompt each time (needed for game traffic and background download monitoring). UAC asks once when this is turned on; a task is created in Task Scheduler that GCM is started through. Turning it off removes the task.

app.rearrange_cards_help: Discards the manual placement of cards into columns; the cards are dealt out in their order again.
app.rereads_the_language_files_from: Rereads the language files from the folders (after you edited or added one).
app.route_tracing_and_the_speed: Route tracing and the speed test only run on demand (Start / Run test button), so they need no switch.
app.saves_the_english_texts_with_all: Saves the English texts with all keys as _template.json into the languages folder. Fill in @meta, translate the values and rename the file to <code>.json.
app.shortcut_help: A global shortcut works anywhere in Windows, also while the window is hidden in the system tray: it brings the GCM window to the front, and pressed again while the window is in front it hides it. It must contain Ctrl or Alt.
app.shown_only_when_advanced_traffic: Shown only when "Advanced traffic monitoring" is on for some game (Game services tab).
app.shown_only_when_the_feature: Shown only when the feature is turned on (Settings › Modules).
app.shows_a_yes_no_question_when: Shows a Yes / No question when you close the window with the cross or choose Exit.
app.the_app_starts_hidden_in: the app starts hidden in the system tray
app.the_change_applies_immediately_inclu: The change applies immediately, including the tray icon menu.
app.the_dashboard_is_empty_add: The dashboard is empty – add cards via "Customize".
app.the_feature_is_turned_off: The feature is turned off (Settings › Modules).

app.the_shortcut_needs_ctrl_or_alt: The shortcut must contain Ctrl or Alt and a letter, digit or F key.
app.updates_have_not_been_checked: Updates have not been checked yet.
compare.both_the_route_to_the: Both the route to the server and the reference target fail starting at your router (hop 1). Check the cable or Wi-Fi, network load (downloads, other devices streaming) and the router.
compare.both_the_route_to_the_2: Both the route to the server and the reference target fail at the same time{}. The problem is with your internet connection (provider), not the game.
compare.loss_or_delays_appeared_on: Loss or delays appeared on the route to the game servers{}, while the reference target was fine. The problem is outside your PC and home network – at a provider on the route or just before the server. You can only wait; a different game region sometimes helps.
compare.network_is_fine_game_or: network is fine – game or server issue
compare.network_is_fine_up_to: network is fine up to hop {} – cause beyond it or in the game
compare.orange_server_grey_reference_red: orange: server · grey: reference · red: loss
compare.problem_on_the_route_to: problem on the route to the game servers
compare.stretches_of_loss_or_latency: Stretches of loss or latency spikes at the end of the route to the game. What matters is whether the game noticed: an anomaly without a flow stall has no effect on the game, and when the reference degraded too it is more likely your connection than the route to the game.
compare.the_game_server_has_an: The game server has an IPv6 address – route measurement is not available for it yet.
compare.the_reference_target_had_trouble: The reference target had trouble, the route to the game servers did not – it does not affect the game.
compare.the_route_to_the_game: The route to the game servers and the reference target have no loss or notable delays.
compare.the_route_to_the_game_2: The route to the game servers up to hop {} and the reference target have no loss or notable delays. The game server does not answer ping, so the part after hop {} is not measured.
compare.the_route_to_the_game_3: The route to the game servers and the reference target had no loss at that time, yet the game stopped receiving data. The cause is most likely on the game server's side or in the game itself (loading, reconnecting, PC load). It is not the network.
compare.the_route_to_the_game_4: The route to the game servers (up to hop {}) and the reference target had no loss at that time, yet the game stopped receiving data. The game server does not answer ping, so the part after hop {} cannot be measured. The cause is either in that part (at a provider or right before the server) or on the game server's side or in the game itself (loading, reconnecting, PC load). It is not your home network or your connection to the provider.
compare.the_route_was_not_being: The route was not being measured at that time (measuring starts once the game server is found) or samples are still missing.
compare.the_server_does_not_answer: the server does not answer ping – the route up to hop {}{} is evaluated
compare.tracing_the_route_to_the: Tracing the route to the new server {} – measuring the current route continues.
compare.trouble_only_on_the_reference: trouble only on the reference target
compare.waiting_for_the_game_server: waiting for the game server to be found
dnsdiag.additional_dns_servers_for_examp: Additional DNS servers (IPv4, separated by commas), e.g. the DNS of your provider. They are used in the check and in the permanent monitoring.
dnsdiag.both_the_dns_servers_and: The DNS servers and Windows both resolve names.
dnsdiag.checks_whether_the_whole_interne: Checks whether the whole internet is down, only your DNS servers, or only name resolution in Windows. Takes a few seconds.
dnsdiag.direct_connections_work_but_no: Direct connections by IP address work, but no DNS server answers directly, neither yours nor the public ones. Typical causes: a firewall, VPN or router that blocks DNS (port 53). Try the repair; if it does not help, check the VPN / firewall.
dnsdiag.dns_servers_answer_directly_but: The DNS servers answer directly, but Windows does not resolve names. Typical causes: a damaged DNS cache, a VPN or the hosts file. Flushing the cache usually helps.
dnsdiag.even_direct_connections_to_ip: Even direct connections to IP addresses fail, so the whole internet connection is down, not just DNS. Check the cable / Wi-Fi, the router and your provider (see the connection status below).
dnsdiag.flushes_the_dns_cache_registers: Flushes the DNS cache (ipconfig /flushdns), re-registers DNS (/registerdns) and renews the IP address from DHCP (/renew; the connection may drop for a few seconds). Then repeats the check.
dnsdiag.more_dns_servers: Include these additional servers in the check:
dnsdiag.no_dns_server_answers_but: No DNS server answers, but the internet works
dnsdiag.no_dns_server_is_set: no DNS server is set in Windows
dnsdiag.no_internet_connection_not_a: No internet connection (not a DNS problem)
dnsdiag.programs_resolve_names_but_these: Programs resolve names, but the listed servers did not answer in the check (wrong address or the server is down).
dnsdiag.public_and_own_dns_servers: Public and your own DNS servers
dnsdiag.public_dns_servers_answer_yours: The public DNS servers answer, but your system DNS does not and Windows cannot resolve names. The repair can help (renewing gets fresh DNS settings from the router). If not, set a public DNS (e.g. 1.1.1.1) in the adapter settings or restart the router.
dnsdiag.repair_done_dns_cache_flushed_dn: Repair done (DNS cache flushed, DNS registered, IP renewed). The result below is from a new check.
dnsdiag.windows_did_not_resolve_the_test: Windows did not resolve the test names
dnsdiag.your_dns_server_router_provider: Your DNS server (router / provider) does not work, the internet does
dnsmon.24_h_and_7_day: 24 h and 7 day availability comes from checks stored in the database (only while the app was running). System DNS = server from Windows settings (at home usually the router forwarding queries to the ISP's DNS).
dnsmon.automatically_every_30_s_even: · automatically every 30 s, even with the window hidden
dnsmon.failed_checks_since_the_app: Failed checks since the app started.
dnsmon.no_dns_responds_probably_a: No DNS responds – probably a connection outage.
dnsmon.start_first_failed_check_end: Start = first failed check, end = first successful one (checks every 30 s, ±30 s accuracy). If the app exited during an outage, the end is the time of the last check.
dnsmon.the_system_dns_is_much: The system DNS is much slower than public DNS.
dnsmon.the_system_dns_responds_now: The system DNS responds now, but had an outage in the last 24 h (see outage history).
dnsmon.the_system_dns_router_isp: The system DNS (router / ISP) does not respond while public DNS does – the problem is the ISP's DNS or the router. Setting public DNS (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8) in the router or Windows helps.
dnsmon.the_system_dns_works_but_these: The system DNS works (programs resolve names), but these monitored servers do not respond: {}
downloads.also_without_a_game_only_above: Works without a game too, but then the separate "Threshold without a game" applies. While a game is running the threshold above applies.
downloads.chooses_the_program_exe_of_a: Choose the program (.exe) of a game that GCM does not know yet.
downloads.click_to_sort: Click to sort by this column.
downloads.free_help: Used in the "always" mode when GCM does not recognize a running game (the higher of the two thresholds applies). Notifications about different programs are also at least 5 minutes apart.
downloads.highest_speed_in_one_second: Highest speed measured in one second since monitoring started. Click to sort.
downloads.hold_help: The speed must stay above the threshold this long, so a short spike does not trigger a notification.
downloads.my_games_help: GCM recognizes games by the name of the running program. Add a game here if it is missing from the known games or cannot be recognized automatically.
downloads.needs_administrator_rights: Seeing which program downloads needs administrator rights.
downloads.repeat_help: Earliest time for another notification about the same program.
downloads.shows_which_programs_and_servi: Programs and Windows services that receive data right now, with the service name inside svchost.exe and the server.
downloads.the_list_refreshes_every_s: The list refreshes every {} s; the speeds are averages over that time.
downloads.threshold_help: Notify when a program other than the game receives more than this speed (average over 5 s).
downloads.while_playing_it_is_downloadin: While playing {}, {} is downloading at {}. This can disturb the game.
downloads.windows_may_hide_notifications: Windows may hide notifications while you play in full screen (Do not disturb / Focus assist). The record below stays.
downloads.works_while_a_game_is_running: Works while a game is running: one monitored in Game services, one from the list of known games, or one of My games. The game itself and GCM are never reported.
features.query_to_the_system_and: Query to the system and public DNS servers every 30 s and storing outages in the database.
features.reachability_of_each_game_servi: Reachability of each game service every 5 s and official status (Xbox, PlayStation) every 2 min.
features.reading_the_network_adapter_sta: Reading the network adapter status (speed, traffic, errors, Wi-Fi signal) every 2 s.
features.shows_which_programs_and_window: Shows which programs and Windows services download data, how much and from which server, and can warn you during a game. Needs administrator rights.
features.windows_services_every_5_s: Windows services every 5 s, NAT type, UPnP, Teredo and Xbox Live reachability every 5 min, official Xbox Live status every 2 min.

flow.the_game_switched_to_another: The game switched to another server (zone, instance or world change). The traffic pause that goes with it is expected and is not counted as an outage.

hopinfo.a_latency_spike_on_the: {}× a latency spike on the target – a short lag in games. Avg {}.
hopinfo.and_the_next_hop_has: and the next hop has {} % loss
hopinfo.last_node_that_answers_the: – last node that answers (the target does not answer ping)
hopinfo.latency_spikes_also_appear_on: Latency spikes also appear on the target at the same moments – the delay originates on this or an earlier part of the route.
hopinfo.lost_on_the_target_at: Lost on the target at the same time:
hopinfo.occasional_latency_spikes_on_thi: Occasional latency spikes on this hop only have the same cause – the router answers ping with low priority. They do not carry over to the target, so they do not affect games.
hopinfo.of_packets_to_the_target: {} % of packets to the target are lost. In games this shows as stutter, rubber-banding or voice dropouts. Check from which hop the losses start (status PROBLEM).
hopinfo.of_the_missing_replies_coincided: {} of the {} missing replies coincided with a loss on the target – this may be a real problem on this part of the route. Effect: lag and dropouts in games.
hopinfo.on_the_target_at_the: {} (on the target at the same time: {})
hopinfo.the_hop_replies_reliably_without: The hop replies reliably, without loss.
hopinfo.the_router_on_this_hop: The router on this hop does not answer every probe (blue lines) – it protects itself from overload by limiting replies to ping. Your data pass through it without loss: the target lost nothing at the same moments{}. It has no effect on games or connection speed – you can ignore the blue lines.
hopinfo.the_target_never_answers_probes: The target never answers probes. That is common for game servers and cloud services (firewall) and not an outage – the last node that answers is evaluated instead.
hopinfo.the_target_replies_reliably_the: The target replies reliably – the connection is fine.
hopinfo.this_router_does_not_answer: This router does not answer probes at all. That is a common setting of ISP routers and not an outage – traffic passes through it normally, as the following hops show. You can ignore it.
hopinfo.while_two_targets_are_measured: While two targets are measured at once, the router gets twice as many probes, hence more blue lines ({} % vs {} %).
hopinfo.your_home_router_does_not: Your home router does not answer this measurement at all because another target is measured at the same time. The router replies only to a limited number of probes (about one per second) and the first measurement gets them. This is not an outage – data pass through the router normally, as the following hops show. No effect on games, you can ignore it.
hopinfo.your_home_router_does_not_2: Your home router does not answer probes (disabled or strongly limited). This is not an outage – data pass through it normally, as the following hops show. No effect on games, you can ignore it.
langs.language_download_is_off_no: Language download is off (no update address set).
limiter.applies_only_to_programs_that_us: Applies only to programs that use Delivery Optimization (Windows Update, Store, Game Pass). Steam, Epic and browsers are not affected – limit them in the programs themselves. Setting the limit restarts the Delivery Optimization service, so a running download pauses briefly. Works only while monitoring is running, because that is how a game is recognized.
limiter.limits_the_speed_of_delivery_opt: Limits the speed of Delivery Optimization, which downloads Windows Update, Microsoft Store and Xbox / Game Pass content. The original Windows setting is restored when the game ends or GCM closes.
limiter.needs_administrator_rights: Changing the limit needs administrator rights.
limiter.registry_error: Could not write the Windows policy (error {}).
limiter.waiting_for_a_game: Waiting for a game to start.
limiter.when_to_limit_help: The limit is applied when GCM recognizes a running game and the original Windows settings are restored when it ends.
limiter.windows_downloads_limited_to: Windows downloads are limited to {} Mbit/s.
link.a_cable_is_more_stable: A cable is more stable for gaming – Wi-Fi adds jitter and short dropouts under interference.
link.asks_the_service_api_ipify_org: Asks the service api.ipify.org for your public IP address. Only done when you click; a connection to that server is made.
link.errors_keep_growing_on_the: Errors keep growing on the adapter – check the cable, connector or network driver.
link.weak_wi_fi_signal_move: Weak Wi-Fi signal – move closer to the router or use a cable.
link.windows_withheld_wi_fi_details: Windows withheld Wi-Fi details – allow location access for desktop apps in Settings › Privacy › Location.
link.your_provider_shares_one_public_add: Your provider shares one public address between customers (CGNAT). This limits incoming connections and the NAT type.
official.reachability_of_addresses_is_ch: Reachability of {} addresses is checked directly from your connection (the provider publishes no status page).
profiles.no_profile_address_set_using: No profile address set – using the built-in ones.
profiles.profiles_need_a_newer_app: profiles need a newer app version (format {})
servers.addresses_and_the_status_source: Addresses and the status source come from the profile and are updated with it.
servers.any_address_and_port_check: Any address and port, check interval and optionally an official status source (e.g. Statuspage).
servers.chooses_the_program_exe_of: Chooses the program (.exe) of the game or app manually in case automatic detection does not find it. The chosen program is added to the manual list.
servers.empty_whole_page_ids_separated: empty = whole page; ids separated by commas
servers.enter_an_address_to_measure: Enter an address to measure or an official status source.
servers.finds_the_running_app_process: Finds the running app (process from the profile) and reads system network events for it only: download, upload and the server it connects to. Packet contents are not read and the app is not touched. Requires administrator rights. The result is on the Dashboard in the "App traffic" card.
servers.finds_the_running_game_process: Finds the running game (process from the profile) and reads system network events for it only: download, upload, game server and flow stalls. Packet contents are not read and the game is not touched. Requires administrator rights. The result is on the Dashboard in the "Game traffic" card.
servers.goes_back_to_the_processes: Goes back to the processes from the profile.
servers.log_help: Opens the log of changes for this game / service in its own tab.
servers.measures_the_route_to_the: Measures the route to the detected game server and to a reference target ({}) and, when the flow stalls, tells where the cause is: on the route to the server, in the home network / at the provider, or in the game. Adds background route measurement (not stored in the database).
servers.name: Name:
servers.no_services_add_a_game: No services – add a game or your own service.
servers.not_available_the_provider_has: not available (the provider has no public API)
servers.nothing_found_you_can_add: Nothing found. You can add the game as a custom service.
servers.nothing_is_measured_game_server: nothing is measured – game server addresses are unknown
servers.number_of_the_server_world: Number of the server (world) to measure: {}–{}. Type the number and press Enter.
servers.official_status_comes_from_the: Official status comes from the provider's public status page. Measured status is reachability from your connection – for games where only the sign-in server is known it shows sign-in availability, not game quality. Comparing both shows whether the problem is the service or the route.
servers.refresh_only_this_service_offici: Refresh only this service (official status and measurement)
servers.show_monitoring_on_dashboard_hel: Shows or hides the advanced monitoring of this service in the Monitoring card on the Dashboard. Monitoring continues either way.
servers.show_status_on_dashboard: Show status in the Services card
servers.show_status_on_dashboard_help: Shows or hides this service in the simple Services card on the Dashboard. Measuring continues either way.
servers.status_cannot_be_verified_follow: Status cannot be verified – follow the provider's links.
servers.the_profile_is_no_longer: The profile is no longer in the definitions – remove the item or add it again.
servers.the_provider_reports_everything_: The provider reports everything is fine.
servers.the_provider_reports_issues_but: The provider reports issues, but your connection to the service is fine.
servers.the_provider_reports_issues_too: The provider reports issues too – the service itself has a problem.
servers.the_provider_reports_no_issues: The provider reports no issues – the problem is likely on the route or in your connection. Try the Route tab.
servers.the_service_is_poorly_reachable: The service is poorly reachable from your network. No official status – check the provider's page.
servers.trace_the_route_to_this: Trace the route to this service
servers.turn_on_advanced_traffic_monitor: Turn on advanced traffic monitoring first.
servers.use_a_different_reference_server: Use a different reference server for this service only. The field is prefilled with the global address from Settings; leave it empty to go back to the global one.
speedtest.bufferbloat_help: Bufferbloat = how much your ping rises when the line is fully used by a download or upload. The more it rises, the more a game lags when someone on the network downloads. Grade A+ (best) to F.
speedtest.latency_increase_under_full_lo: Latency increase under full load. A+/A = the line handles load without lag, C or worse = ping in games rises while downloading (updates, streaming) – SQM / QoS on the router helps.
speedtest.the_test_downloads_and_uploads: The test downloads and uploads data for 2 × 10 s (hundreds of MB on a fast line). If a server does not respond, pick another one.
speedtest.the_test_server_does_not: The test server does not respond – try another one.
status.all_measured_services_are_down: All measured game services are down at once
status.enable_logging_help: Nothing is recorded for a game / service until you turn this on.
status.errors_on_the_link: Errors on the link (dropped packets are increasing)
status.game_crashed: {}: Windows recorded an application crash (event 1000) · exception code {}
status.game_hung: {}: Windows recorded that the program stopped responding (event 1002)
status.internet_is_not_available: Internet is not available (link is down)
status.log_help: Changes and problems of the game / service are recorded here (the last 5000 entries of all games and services are kept, older ones are overwritten).
status.logging_off: Logging is off for this game / service – nothing is being recorded.
status.no_entries: No entries for this game / service yet.
tools.continuous_monitoring_of_the_dns_s: Continuous monitoring of the DNS servers. Turn it on only temporarily to track down a problem with a particular DNS.
tools.the_feature_is_turned_off: The feature is turned off in Settings › Modules – nothing is measured.
trace.at_the_set_interval_1: At the set interval (1 s by default) the app pings each router (hop) on the way to the target. What matters for games is the target – a problem on a hop is real only if it continues on the following hops and on the target.
trace.automatic_target_controlled_by_the: automatic target – controlled by the game's "Comparison with the route" option (Game services tab), it cannot be edited or stopped here
trace.average_response_time_of_the: average response time of the hop.
trace.colour_overview_of_the_last: Colour overview of the last 150 samples of all hops below the graph.
trace.dashed_vertical_markers_in_the: Dashed vertical markers in the hop graph: measurement start, stop and pause, interval change, quick jitter test, speed test, DNS outage – to see what was happening at that moment. Number = events since the app started.
trace.does_not_answer_ping_common: does not answer ping (common for game servers)
trace.enter_a_target_ip_or: Enter a target (IP or DNS name) and click Start or press Enter.
trace.events_measurement_start_stop_and: events (measurement start, stop and pause, interval change, jitter test, speed test, DNS outage) – can be turned off.
trace.green_up_to_100_ms: green up to 100 ms, yellow 100–200 ms, red above 200 ms. The scale is in the header on the right.
trace.hop_orange_dots_elevated_latency: Hop {} – orange dots = elevated latency (> {} ms), red lines = real loss (also on the target), blue lines = the hop just did not reply (harmless). Wheel = zoom, drag = pan, double-click = whole window.
trace.how_much_the_response_time: how much the response time varies between consecutive pings (over the graph window). For games: up to 15 ms fine, above 30 ms noticeable.
trace.how_often_each_hop_is: How often each hop is measured. Pick a preset or type your own value (e.g. 45 min, 1000 ms, 0.5 s) and press Enter – it is saved to the list. The change applies immediately, also to running measurements (marked as an event in the graph).
trace.latency_jitter_loss_and_no: Latency, Jitter, Loss and No reply columns are over the last {}; Avg / Min / Max since the start. Detailed description of all marks and colours: „Help“ button or click the Latency header.
trace.latency_spike_a_single_ping: latency spike – a single ping whose RTT exceeded the threshold 2 × the hop minimum + 25 ms (shown above the graph). Hover to see the exact value. How to read them: a few isolated dots are normal and barely noticeable in games. Many dots in a short time = stuttering (lag spikes). The target decides: if spikes appear only on an intermediate hop and the target has none at the same moment, the router just delays ping replies (harmless). If the target has them too, the delay is real – and the hop from which they appear and continue to the target shows where the problem starts. Spikes during a speed test or a download usually mean your own line is overloaded (bufferbloat).
trace.loss_jitter_or_high_latency: Loss, jitter or high latency on this hop only while the target is fine – the router probably just rate-limits ICMP replies. Traffic is not affected.
trace.loss_jitter_or_high_latency_2: Loss, jitter or high latency also shows on the target – a real problem starting at this hop.
trace.loss_or_delay_only_on: loss or delay only on this hop, the target is fine – the router just limits ping replies.
trace.mouse_wheel_zoom_drag_pan: Mouse wheel = zoom, drag = pan, double-click = back to the whole window. Below the graph is the Hop analysis with a plain-language verdict.
trace.name: Name
trace.no_events_in_the_shown: No events in the shown range (start/stop of another target, quick jitter test, speed test, DNS outage).
trace.over_the_graph_window_often: Over the graph window. Often distorted on intermediate hops by ICMP rate limiting – the target's jitter is what counts.
trace.pings_to_the_target_every: {} pings to the target every {} ms (~{} s) – a finer jitter than the regular per-second measurement.
trace.range_from_the_lowest_to: range from the lowest to the highest response time of the hop.
trace.real_loss_over_the_graph: Real loss over the graph window: the packet was also lost on the target. Affects games (lag, dropouts).
trace.real_loss_the_packet_was: real loss – the packet was also lost on the target. This affects games (lag, rubber-banding, voice dropouts).
trace.response_time_over_time_averaged: response time over time (averaged for long windows).
trace.response_time_rtt_of_the: response time (RTT) of the hop; avg, min and max since the start.
trace.row_hop_column_one_sample: Row = hop, column = one sample (newest on the right, last 150). The latency colour is relative to each hop: green = close to its lowest latency, red = above the spike threshold (2 × minimum + 25 ms).
trace.rtt_round_trip_time_is: RTT (Round-Trip Time) is the time in milliseconds a packet takes to reach a router or the target and for the reply to come back. In games it is called ping or latency. The lower, the faster the game reacts: up to ~30 ms excellent, 30–60 ms good, 60–100 ms noticeable, above 100 ms disturbing (especially in shooters and fighting games). Stability matters too – RTT variation is jitter.
trace.share_of_real_loss_unanswered: share of real loss / unanswered pings (length = percentage of the width).
trace.some_routers_on_the_route: Some routers on the route rate-limit ICMP replies – traffic is not affected.
trace.start_measuring_first_the_test: Start measuring first – the test needs the resolved target address.
trace.temporarily_stops_measuring_withou: Temporarily stops measuring without losing data; Resume continues in the same graph.
trace.the_green_red_gradient_shows: The green » red gradient shows only how high the latency is. Real loss deliberately has a different colour (purple) so it is not confused with high latency – a lost packet is worse for games than a delayed one. The heatmap can be hidden with „Show heatmap“.
trace.the_hop_averages_in_order: the hop averages in order – where it rises sharply, delay is being added.
trace.the_hop_did_not_answer: the hop did not answer the probe, but traffic passed. Routers limit ping replies to protect themselves – harmless, no effect on games.
trace.the_hop_did_not_answer_2: The hop did not answer the probe but traffic passed (the target lost nothing at that moment). Typically a router limiting ping replies – harmless, no effect on games.
trace.the_hop_just_did_not: the hop just did not reply – harmless.
trace.the_hop_responds_without_loss: The hop responds without loss and with usual latency.
trace.the_node_never_answers_ping: The node never answers ping (firewall, ICMP disabled) – common for game servers and cloud. It is not an outage, traffic passes through; the nodes that do answer are evaluated instead.
trace.the_route_to_is_measured: The route to {} is measured – it ends at the same node as the route to the new server, so measuring continues without a break.
trace.the_trouble_also_shows_on: the trouble also shows on the target – a real problem starts at this hop.
trace.what_do_the_marks_in: What do the marks in this column mean? Click for help.
trace.what_the_columns_marks_and: What the columns, marks and colours mean

xbox.sets_teredo_to_the_windows: Sets Teredo to the Windows default mode (netsh interface teredo set state type=default). Needed for Xbox party chat and some P2P games in the Xbox app.
xbox.to_start_stop_or_restart: To start, stop or restart services, run the application as administrator.
